s: A company is evaluating cost optimization opportunities across its AWS environment. The team has discovered that several production workloads are significantly over-provisioned, spending approximately $2.4M annually on unused compute capacity. Additionally, the organization has unpredictable batch processing jobs that run on-demand and inconsistent database utilization patterns. The CFO requires clear cost visibility and predictable spending without sacrificing performance. Which combination of strategies would provide the greatest cost optimization with appropriate cost visibility?
o: Use Compute Savings Plans for baseline production compute, Spot Instances for batch jobs with interruption tolerance, enable AWS Cost Anomaly Detection, and implement chargeback via Cost Allocation Tags
Migrate all workloads to Graviton-based instances, consolidate databases into shared RDS instances, reduce backup retention, and disable detailed CloudWatch metrics
Purchase 3-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for all production workloads and database instances to achieve maximum discount rates
Implement aggressive auto-scaling based on CPU utilization, terminate underutilized instances after 30 days of low usage, and use the AWS Pricing Calculator for monthly forecasts
e: The correct answer is the first option. It directly addresses both cost optimization and visibility requirements: Compute Savings Plans provide 20-25% discounts for baseline production workloads while maintaining flexibility if demand changes. Spot Instances for batch jobs deliver up to 90% discounts for interruptible workloads. Cost Anomaly Detection provides automated visibility into unexpected cost changes. Cost Allocation Tags enable chargeback to business units, driving accountability for spending. The second option makes architectural changes (Graviton, consolidation, reduced backups) that may harm performance and don't address the core over-provisioning problem. The third option locks the organization into 3-year commitments on potentially over-provisioned infrastructure - if workloads are currently over provisioned, this amplifies waste. The fourth option doesn't leverage purchasing discounts and relies on reactive termination rather than proactive capacity planning. This question tests cost optimization and visibility strategies, which are explicit SAP-C02 objectives under organizational complexity.

w.y: The goals are cut waste, handle unpredictable batch jobs cheaply, and give the CFO visibility and predictable spend. Compute Savings Plans cover the steady baseline across instance types, Spot fits interruptible batch jobs, Cost Anomaly Detection flags surprises, and cost allocation tags enable chargeback.

o.A: Correct: Savings Plans for baseline, Spot for batch, anomaly detection and tag-based chargeback.
o.B: Shared databases, shorter backups and fewer metrics risk performance and give no cost visibility.
o.C: 3-year RIs for over-provisioned workloads lock in the waste.
o.D: Terminating instances after 30 days and the Pricing Calculator do not give real visibility or predictability.
